item.title: 15 Art Excursions Outside NYC This Spring
item.description: The avant-garde environments of Piero Manzoni, the abstract visions of Agnes Martin, Rina Banerjee’s diaphanous monuments, and so much else to see.

item.title: How to Heal Your Creative Hangover
item.description: Long-lost Rembrandt goes on view, 3D scans of The Met's treasures, spring shows outside NYC, and how to cure the emotional crash after artistic bursts.

item.title: Interdimensional Timelines: Hartford Art School Exhibits Liz Nielsen’s Photograms
item.description: As she concludes her term as the university’s Distinguished Chair in Photography, Nielsen’s “light paintings” are on view this spring in West Hartford, Connecticut.

item.title: A View From the Easel
item.description: “I work as an attorney during the day and let loose at night in my studio.”

item.title: Olafur Eliasson: A symphony of disappearing sounds for the Great Salt Lake
item.description: As the lake’s ecological crisis worsens, the artist’s new site-specific installation in Salt Lake City renders audible what is increasingly at risk of vanishing.

item.title: Guggenheim Union Rallies at Carol Bove Reception
item.description: “We're out here rallying to put pressure on the museum to come back to the bargaining table with a bit more movability on their positions,” said one of the workers.

item.title: The Polycrisis Sublime of the Whitney Biennial
item.description: It felt like the world as I experience it: no clear path, but enough moments of beauty to convince me to put one foot in front of the other.

item.title: Required Reading
item.description: This week: Iranian heritage sites, a Native artist’s anti-ICE beadwork, France’s Braille Museum, mapping Black-owned bookstores, the business behind America’s sauna frenzy, and more.

item.title: Art Movements: Anicka Yi Picks Up the Pace
item.description: The artist is now represented by Pace, along with three other galleries. Plus, NYC has a new culture commissioner, closures at art schools, and more industry news.

item.title: An Overfilled Guggenheim Retrospective Dulls Carol Bove’s Brilliance
item.description: A smaller survey would have allowed for something more meaningful than just showing what Bove has been doing for the past decades.
